assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydro-electricity
items.clue: Uses water stored behind a dam.

items.label: Renewable energy resource
items.clue: One that is replenished as it is used.

items.label: Geothermal
items.clue: Uses hot rock beneath the Earth's surface.

items.label: Nuclear fuel
items.clue: Uranium or plutonium used in power stations.

questions.stem: A student is asked to list the main energy resources available for use on Earth. Which list is correct?

options.text: Nuclear fuel, the tides, geothermal energy and water waves
Bio-fuel, wind, hydro-electricity and mains electricity
Coal, oil, gas and electricity from the mains
The Sun, wind turbines, the tides and bio-fuel crops

questions.explanation: All four appear in the specification's list of the main energy resources available for use on Earth.

questions.stem: Where does the energy supplied by a geothermal resource come from?

options.text: From sunlight that has warmed the ground during the day
From the hot rock lying deep below the Earth's surface
From fossil fuels that are burning deep underground
From fuel steadily burning deep within the Earth

questions.explanation: Geothermal energy is the energy of hot rock underground, which is why it is available at all hours and in any weather.

questions.stem: Which statement is the specification's definition of a renewable energy resource?

options.text: One with a supply so large that it could never all be used up
One that gives off no carbon dioxide while it is being used
One that is being, or can be, replenished as it is used
One that costs nothing to use once it has been built

questions.explanation: This is the definition word for word: replacement keeping pace with use.

questions.stem: Nuclear fuel is classified as non-renewable. Which reason for that classification is correct?

options.text: Uranium is mined from rock, so it is a fossil fuel
Nuclear power stations release carbon dioxide as they run
The clouds from its cooling towers add carbon dioxide
The uranium used is not replenished as it is used

questions.explanation: Applies the definition directly: the fuel in the ground is not being replaced as it is consumed.

questions.stem: Why is bio-fuel classified as a renewable energy resource?

options.text: The crops it is made from can be grown again as the fuel is used
It gives off much less carbon dioxide than burning coal does
There is so much plant material that it could never run out
It is made from living things rather than from rock

questions.explanation: The definition is met: the supply is replenished, by replanting, at the rate it is drawn on.

questions.stem: New coal is still slowly forming underground today. Why is coal still classed as non-renewable?

options.text: It is not: coal is renewable because new coal is still forming
New coal is forming far more slowly than it is being used
Coal gives off carbon dioxide, and renewables are clean
Coal supplies will have run out within about ten years

questions.explanation: Replenishment has to keep pace with use. Coal takes millions of years to form and is burned in minutes.

questions.stem: The specification gives three uses of energy resources. Which set of three is correct?

options.text: Transport, electricity generation and lighting
Electricity generation, heating and cooking food
Transport, electricity generation and heating
Heating, lighting and cooking in the home

questions.explanation: These are the three uses named in the specification.

questions.stem: Which energy resource supplies most of the energy used for transport worldwide?

options.text: Electricity from wind farms
Bio-fuel grown from sugar cane
Coal burned in steam engines
Oil, as petrol and diesel

questions.explanation: Transport runs overwhelmingly on oil products; other resources supply only small shares.

questions.stem: Panels on the roof of a house use the Sun to warm the water in a hot water tank. Which use of an energy resource is this?

options.text: Heating, because the Sun's energy is warming the water directly
Electricity generation, because solar panels make electricity
Transport, because that is a common use of energy
Electricity generation, then heating from the mains

questions.explanation: The resource is the Sun and the job being done is heating; no electricity is involved at any point.

questions.stem: Which group of resources is used for all three of transport, electricity generation and heating?

options.text: Wind, which could drive vehicles, power stations and radiators
Fossil fuels, which are burned for all three of these jobs
The tides, which run at all hours and serve every use
Nuclear fuel, used in stations, cars and in boilers

questions.explanation: Oil fuels transport, gas and coal generate electricity, and gas and oil heat buildings.

questions.stem: Why is a wind farm a less reliable energy resource than a gas-fired power station?

options.text: It is not less reliable, because the wind never stops blowing
Each turbine gives out less energy than a gas power station
Its output falls when the wind drops, whatever the demand
Wind turbines break down far more often than gas plants

questions.explanation: Reliability is about being available when energy is wanted, and wind output is set by the weather.

questions.stem: Tidal energy is described as a reliable energy resource. Which statement explains why?

options.text: The tides are driven by winds that blow daily
Tidal stations give out more energy than any other
The sea is pushed along by winds that never stop
The tides rise and fall on a known cycle

questions.explanation: The times of high and low water are set by the Moon and the Sun and can be predicted years ahead.
